results.question: Show top 5 employees by salary
results.expected_sql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 5
results.generated_sql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC LIMIT 5;

results.question: What is the total sales revenue?
results.expected_sql: SELECT SUM(total_amount) as total_revenue FROM sales
results.generated_sql: SELECT SUM(total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM sales LIMIT 100;

results.question: Total sales revenue by region
results.expected_sql: SELECT c.region, SUM(s.total_amount) as revenue FROM sales s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.region
results.generated_sql: SELECT c.region, SUM(s.total_amount) AS revenue FROM sales s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.region ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 100;

results.question: Which department has the highest average salary?
results.expected_sql: SELECT d.name, AVG(e.salary) as avg_salary FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id GROUP BY d.name ORDER BY avg_salary DESC LIMIT 1
results.generated_sql: SELECT d.name AS department, AVG(e.salary) AS avg_salary FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id GROUP BY d.name ORDER BY avg_salary DESC LIMIT 1;

results.question: Show me products with low stock
results.expected_sql: SELECT name, stock_quantity FROM products WHERE stock_quantity < 100 ORDER BY stock_quantity ASC
results.generated_sql: SELECT id, name, category, price, stock_quantity FROM products WHERE stock_quantity < 100 LIMIT 100;

results.question: How many employees are in each department?
results.expected_sql: SELECT d.name as department, COUNT(e.id) as employee_count FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id GROUP BY d.name
results.generated_sql: SELECT d.name AS department, COUNT(e.id) AS employee_count FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id GROUP BY d.name LIMIT 100;

results.question: List all customers from North America
results.expected_sql: SELECT name, company, join_date FROM customers WHERE region = 'North America'
results.generated_sql: SELECT * FROM customers WHERE region = 'North America' LIMIT 100;

results.question: Who are the top 3 salespeople by total revenue?
results.expected_sql: SELECT e.name, SUM(s.total_amount) as total_revenue FROM sales s JOIN employees e ON s.employee_id = e.id GROUP BY e.name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 3
results.generated_sql: SELECT e.name AS salesperson, SUM(s.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM sales s JOIN employees e ON s.employee_id = e.id GROUP BY e.name ORDER BY total_revenue DESC LIMIT 3;

results.question: What is the most expensive product?
results.expected_sql: SELECT name, price FROM products ORDER BY price DESC LIMIT 1
results.generated_sql: SELECT name, MAX(price) AS max_price FROM products LIMIT 1;

results.question: Show monthly sales trends
results.expected_sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(sale_date, '%Y-%m') as month, SUM(total_amount) as revenue FROM sales GROUP BY month ORDER BY month
results.generated_sql: SELECT DATE_FORMAT(s.sale_date, '%Y-%m') AS month, SUM(s.total_amount) AS total_revenue FROM sales s GROUP BY month ORDER BY month ASC LIMIT 100;

results.question: Which product category generates the most revenue?
results.expected_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(s.total_amount) as revenue FROM sales s JOIN products p ON s.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY revenue DESC
results.generated_sql: SELECT p.category, SUM(s.total_amount) AS revenue FROM sales s JOIN products p ON s.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.category ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 1;

results.question: List employees hired in the last year
results.expected_sql: SELECT name, hire_date, role FROM employees WHERE hire_date >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 1 YEAR)
results.generated_sql: SELECT name, email, hire_date FROM employees WHERE hire_date >= DATE_SUB(CURDATE(), INTERVAL 1 YEAR) LIMIT 100;

results.question: Compare sales between North America and Europe
results.expected_sql: SELECT c.region, COUNT(s.sale_id) as num_sales, SUM(s.total_amount) as total_revenue FROM sales s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.id WHERE c.region IN ('North America', 'Europe') GROUP BY c.region
results.generated_sql: SELECT c.region, SUM(s.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM sales s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.id WHERE c.region IN ('North America', 'Europe') GROUP BY c.region ORDER BY total_sales DESC LIMIT 100;

results.question: Show departments and their total budget
results.expected_sql: SELECT name, budget, location FROM departments ORDER BY budget DESC
results.generated_sql: SELECT name AS department, SUM(budget) AS total_budget FROM departments GROUP BY name LIMIT 100;

results.question: What is the average order value?
results.expected_sql: SELECT AVG(total_amount) as avg_order_value FROM sales
results.generated_sql: SELECT AVG(total_amount) AS average_order_value FROM sales LIMIT 100;

results.question: Which customers have made the most purchases?
results.expected_sql: SELECT c.name, c.company, COUNT(s.sale_id) as purchase_count, SUM(s.total_amount) as total_spent FROM sales s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.id, c.name, c.company ORDER BY purchase_count DESC LIMIT 10
results.generated_sql: SELECT c.name, COUNT(s.id) AS purchase_count FROM customers c JOIN sales s ON c.id = s.customer_id GROUP BY c.name ORDER BY purchase_count DESC LIMIT 100;

results.question: Show all managers and their salaries
results.expected_sql: SELECT name, salary, department_id FROM employees WHERE role LIKE '%Manager%' OR role LIKE '%Director%' ORDER BY salary DESC
results.generated_sql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE role = 'Manager' LIMIT 100;

results.question: What percentage of total sales comes from each region?
results.expected_sql: SELECT c.region, SUM(s.total_amount) as revenue, ROUND(SUM(s.total_amount) * 100.0 / (SELECT SUM(total_amount) FROM sales), 2) as percentage FROM sales s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.region ORDER BY percentage DESC
results.generated_sql: SELECT c.region, (SUM(s.total_amount) / (SELECT SUM(total_amount) FROM sales)) * 100 AS percentage_of_total_sales FROM sales s JOIN customers c ON s.customer_id = c.id GROUP BY c.region ORDER BY percentage_of_total_sales DESC LIMIT 100;

results.question: Find products that have never been sold
results.expected_sql: SELECT p.name, p.category, p.price FROM products p LEFT JOIN sales s ON p.id = s.product_id WHERE s.sale_id IS NULL
results.generated_sql: SELECT p.id, p.name, p.category, p.price, p.stock_quantity FROM products p LEFT JOIN sales s ON p.id = s.product_id WHERE s.product_id IS NULL LIMIT 100;

results.question: Show the salary distribution across roles
results.expected_sql: SELECT role, COUNT(*) as count, AVG(salary) as avg_salary, MIN(salary) as min_salary, MAX(salary) as max_salary FROM employees GROUP BY role
results.generated_sql: SELECT role, COUNT(*) AS number_of_employees, MIN(salary) AS min_salary, MAX(salary) AS max_salary, AVG(salary) AS avg_salary FROM employees GROUP BY role ORDER BY avg_salary DESC LIMIT 100;

results.question: Show all employees
results.expected_sql: SELECT * FROM employees LIMIT 100
results.generated_sql: SELECT * FROM employees LIMIT 100;

results.question: How many products do we have in each category?
results.expected_sql: SELECT category, COUNT(*) as product_count FROM products GROUP BY category ORDER BY product_count DESC
results.generated_sql: SELECT category, COUNT(*) AS product_count FROM products GROUP BY category LIMIT 100;

results.question: What are the top selling products by quantity?
results.expected_sql: SELECT p.name, SUM(s.quantity) as total_sold FROM sales s JOIN products p ON s.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.name ORDER BY total_sold DESC LIMIT 10
results.generated_sql: SELECT p.name AS product_name, SUM(s.quantity) AS total_quantity_sold FROM sales s JOIN products p ON s.product_id = p.id GROUP BY p.name ORDER BY total_quantity_sold DESC LIMIT 100;

results.question: Show me employees who earn more than 80000
results.expected_sql: SELECT name, salary, department_id FROM employees WHERE salary > 80000 ORDER BY salary DESC
results.generated_sql: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE salary > 80000 LIMIT 100;

results.question: What is the revenue per employee?
results.expected_sql: SELECT e.name, SUM(s.total_amount) as revenue FROM employees e LEFT JOIN sales s ON e.id = s.employee_id GROUP BY e.id, e.name ORDER BY revenue DESC
results.generated_sql: SELECT e.name AS employee_name, SUM(s.total_amount) AS revenue FROM employees e LEFT JOIN sales s ON e.id = s.employee_id GROUP BY e.name ORDER BY revenue DESC LIMIT 100;

results.question: Show customers who joined this year
results.expected_sql: SELECT name, company, region, join_date FROM customers WHERE YEAR(join_date) = YEAR(CURDATE()) ORDER BY join_date DESC
results.generated_sql: SELECT name, company, region, join_date FROM customers WHERE YEAR(join_date) = YEAR(CURDATE()) LIMIT 100;

results.question: Which department has the most employees?
results.expected_sql: SELECT d.name as department, COUNT(e.id) as employee_count FROM departments d JOIN employees e ON d.id = e.department_id GROUP BY d.name ORDER BY employee_count DESC LIMIT 1
results.generated_sql: SELECT d.name AS department, COUNT(e.id) AS employee_count FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id GROUP BY d.name ORDER BY employee_count DESC LIMIT 1;

results.question: Show quarterly sales for this year
results.expected_sql: SELECT QUARTER(sale_date) as quarter, SUM(total_amount) as revenue, COUNT(*) as num_sales FROM sales WHERE YEAR(sale_date) = YEAR(CURDATE()) GROUP BY quarter ORDER BY quarter
results.generated_sql: SELECT QUARTER(s.sale_date) AS quarter, SUM(s.total_amount) AS total_sales FROM sales s WHERE YEAR(s.sale_date) = YEAR(CURDATE()) GROUP BY QUARTER(s.sale_date) ORDER BY quarter LIMIT 1000;

results.question: Find the average salary by department ranked highest to lowest
results.expected_sql: SELECT d.name as department, AVG(e.salary) as avg_salary, COUNT(e.id) as headcount FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id GROUP BY d.name ORDER BY avg_salary DESC
results.generated_sql: SELECT d.name AS department, AVG(e.salary) AS avg_salary FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id GROUP BY d.name ORDER BY avg_salary DESC LIMIT 100;

results.question: Show the top 10 most recent sales
results.expected_sql: SELECT s.sale_id, e.name as employee, s.total_amount, s.sale_date FROM sales s JOIN employees e ON s.employee_id = e.id ORDER BY s.sale_date DESC LIMIT 10
results.generated_sql: SELECT * FROM sales ORDER BY sale_date DESC LIMIT 10;

results.question: What is the total number of customers per region?
results.expected_sql: SELECT region, COUNT(*) as customer_count FROM customers GROUP BY region ORDER BY customer_count DESC
results.generated_sql: SELECT region, COUNT(*) AS total_customers FROM customers GROUP BY region ORDER BY total_customers DESC LIMIT 100;

results.question: Show products priced between 50 and 200
results.expected_sql: SELECT name, category, price FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 50 AND 200 ORDER BY price ASC
results.generated_sql: SELECT * FROM products WHERE price BETWEEN 50 AND 200 LIMIT 100;

results.question: Which employees have made no sales?
results.expected_sql: SELECT e.name, e.department_id, e.role FROM employees e LEFT JOIN sales s ON e.id = s.employee_id WHERE s.sale_id IS NULL
results.generated_sql: SELECT name, email FROM employees WHERE id NOT IN (SELECT employee_id FROM sales) LIMIT 1000;

results.question: Show the running total of sales by date
results.expected_sql: SELECT sale_date, SUM(total_amount) as daily_total, SUM(SUM(total_amount)) OVER (ORDER BY sale_date) as running_total FROM sales GROUP BY sale_date ORDER BY sale_date
results.generated_sql: SELECT sale_date, SUM(total_amount) OVER (ORDER BY sale_date) AS running_total FROM sales ORDER BY sale_date LIMIT 100;

results.question: Find departments where average salary exceeds 70000
results.expected_sql: SELECT d.name as department, AVG(e.salary) as avg_salary FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id GROUP BY d.name HAVING AVG(e.salary) > 70000
results.generated_sql: SELECT d.name AS department, AVG(e.salary) AS avg_salary FROM employees e JOIN departments d ON e.department_id = d.id GROUP BY d.name HAVING AVG(e.salary) > 70000 LIMIT 100;
